page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The system features 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include bundled local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a distinct performance profile. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% of stress-ng tests, and Geekbench single-core scores are average. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with read and write speeds in uncached large-block tests categorized as weak. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing perform at average levels, whereas multi-threaded operations such as bzip3 decompression and software compilation show weaker results.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and modest resource footprint, the t2d-standard-2 offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require predictable single-core performance without the overhead of high-density memory or storage. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, including basic web serving, single-threaded background processing, small-scale text processing, and low-concurrency utility services.
